primitives.verbatim_quote: **Isotonic PAVA** — monotone CEP; plateaus can collapse ranking → use CIR when collapse high 2.
primitives.assumptions: Monotonicity constraint on predicted probabilities; empirical data admits piecewise constant CEP structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When plateau regions collapse, ranking becomes ambiguous; requires CIR fallback.

primitives.name: Newton Temperature Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Temperature (Newton NLL)** — global soften/sharpen; primary log-loss lever for overconfidence 3.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\theta': 'temperature scalar (dimensionless)', 'p(y|x, \\theta)': 'scaled softmax probability (dimensionless)', '\\mathbb{E}': 'expectation over data distribution (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Model outputs follow softmax distribution; log-loss is differentiable and convex in temperature parameter.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overconfident predictions lead to divergent NLL; requires Newton iteration convergence.

layer2.mapping: Newton NLL optimization adjusts model confidence globally; aligns with GSE's adaptive state transitions based on calibration feedback.

primitives.name: Cross-Validation Select Calibrator
primitives.verbatim_quote: **CV selectCalibrator** — OOF equal-mass ECE + noise bar (not log-loss objective) 5.
primitives.assumptions: Equal-mass bins ensure uniform coverage; noise bar filters unstable calibrators.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High variance in ECE across folds indicates unreliable calibrator.

layer2.mapping: CV selection mimics GSI’s Bayesian model averaging by choosing best-performing calibrators under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: ECE mean ± std, noise-bar pass/fail ratio

This is essential for preserving rank integrity during inference. When plateaus occur, CIR (Constrained Isotonic Regression) acts as a fallback mechanism to maintain ranking consistency. Newton temperature scaling provides a global adjustment to model confidence by minimizing negative log-likelihood, effectively softening or sharpening the output distribution. The CV-based calibrator selection uses out-of-fold ECE and noise resilience to choose robust models without relying on log-loss alone.
